response.name: Catalog of building blocks
response.summary: One curated catalog of skills, plugins, workflows and approved models, read by every tenant's design and compile path (WS-027).

exposes.why: a tenant must resolve the blocks its design names, and a per-tenant copy would fork review and leave known-bad versions in use
the fabric deprecates an entry only when it knows who is still on it; counts are aggregated and carry no payload

response.failure_impact: No tenant can resolve a building block; compiles fail closed rather than falling back to an unreviewed local copy.

response.name: Identity
response.summary: One issuer for operator and designer principals (ADR-0047). Workload identities inside a tenant are minted per tenant and are deliberately not shared (ADR-0050).

exposes.why: an operator is one person across tenants and an audit trail that cannot join them is not an audit trail

response.failure_impact: Nobody can authenticate to the fabric; already-running tenants keep running on their own workload identities.

response.name: Observability sinks
response.summary: Traces, metrics and audit events from every tenant land in fabric sinks so an operator can answer 'is it healthy' in one place (WS-010).

exposes.what: trace, metric and audit records tagged with tenant id
exposes.why: operations need cross-tenant aggregates; the tenant tag is what keeps a query from reading across the boundary

response.failure_impact: The fabric goes blind: health and drift fall back to belief alone, which health.py reports as unobserved rather than healthy.

response.name: Record layer
response.summary: Decisions and workstreams (ADR-0001) describing the platform all tenants run on, plus the operational record each tenant feeds (WS-014).

exposes.why: the rules a tenant is held to should be readable by the people held to them

response.failure_impact: Operators lose the written reason for a platform behaviour; running tenants are unaffected.
